Plant Parts & Functions

CONCEPT 2
Stems & Support
5 questions
The stem supports the plant to hold the leaves upright. Climbing plants have weak stems and need poles to reach more light.
weak stem more light
CONCEPT 3
Plant Life Cycle
4 questions
A seed germinates into a young plant, which grows into an adult plant. Young plants cannot reproduce until they bear flowers and fruits.
germinate adult plant
CONCEPT 4
Fungi Characteristics
3 questions
Fungi cannot make their own food and feed on the living or dead things they grow on. They reproduce using spores, not seeds.
spores cannot make food
CONCEPT 5
Roots & Stability
3 questions
Longer roots hold the plant more firmly to the ground. This prevents the plant from being easily washed or blown away.
hold firmly longer roots
CONCEPT 6
Living vs Non-living
4 questions
Living things need water, can grow, move, reproduce, and respond to changes. Non-living things cannot do these.
respond to changes reproduce

Why Open-Ended is Harder Than MCQ

Instead of just recognizing facts, you must build complete logical chains using exact vocabulary. For example, if you say a plant climbs to "get sunlight", you lose marks if you do not add the critical outcome: "to make more food".

Common P4 Open-Ended Writing Mistakes

Avoid these frequent errors that cause P4 students to lose marks even when they know the science concepts.

Critical Distinctions for P4

Keywords to Write in Your P4 Answers

Linking Words

In P4 Science, correctly connecting your facts is just as important as the facts themselves. Use BECAUSE to give a reason, BUT / WHEREAS to show a difference, and SO THAT to state an ultimate biological goal (e.g., getting light so that it can make food).

Wrong Written Answers — P4 Traps

Answer Formulas for P4 Plant Systems

Examiners look for specific structures in your answers. Memorise these patterns.

EXPLAIN The "Why" Pattern

Use when asked: "Why does...", "Give a reason..."

Observation + BECAUSE / SO THAT + Scientific Reason (Keyword)

Real Example from a P4 Model Answer:

The rod provides support for the stem to hold the leaves up so that the leaves can get more light to make more food.
What to AVOID:
Avoid skipping the final goal (just saying "to get light" instead of "to make food").
Avoid using general words like "to survive" instead of exact biological processes.

COMPARE The Difference Pattern

Use when asked: "State one difference...", "How are they different..."

Subject A trait + BUT / WHEREAS + Subject B trait

Real Example from a P4 Model Answer:

Q cannot make its own food, but R can make its own food.
What to AVOID:
Avoid describing only one subject (e.g. "Q cannot make food."). You must mention both.
Avoid comparing different axes (e.g. "Q is small but R makes food.").

STATE The Direct Fact Pattern

Use when asked: "State...", "Name...", "Identify..."

Subject + Specific Science Fact

Real Example from a P4 Model Answer:

M can make its own food, but N gets food from living things it grows on.
What to AVOID:
Avoid writing long stories. Get straight to the keyword fact.

Universal Open-Ended Answer Checklist

✓ Did I use the exact keyword (e.g. "absorb water", not "drink")?
✓ If asking "Why", did I trace it to the final goal (make more food)?
✓ If comparing, did I mention BOTH items explicitly?
✓ Did I copy data directly from the table/graph without changing units?
✓ Have I used linking words (because, so that, but) clearly?
